Last Friday (21st) in the verdict of the Hong Kong Alliance case, during the early morning hours, police escorted a woman who was queuing for a seat in the public gallery onto a police vehicle and took her away. In response to enquiries, the police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges, including "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or deliberately obstructing police officers in the execution of their duties", and "seditious intent".

At around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than 50 people had already queued outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During the queue, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue "appeared to have something slightly seditious about her clothing" and took her onto a police vehicle and left. While the officers were taking the woman away, several officers kept directing reporters to leave, saying "take you to the press area", and pulled the orange cordon towards the direction of Ying Wa Street. After the woman boarded the police vehicle, they put away the cordon. On that day, a "court-watcher" who was queuing near the woman said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

"集誌社" (The Collective) enquired with the police about why the woman was taken away and whether the police had made an arrest. In a reply this morning (24th), the police stated that during a security operation conducted in the vicinity of the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts on 21 August, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or deliberately obstructing police officers in the execution of their duties", and "seditious intent", and was detained for investigation.
